title: Even using Legend for a week now
body:
Legend is nice if you trade from your desktop and use the Robinhood $HOOD ecosystem.

Pros
- Great UI
- Can exit, sell, and buy options directly in the platform
- No more context switching 
- Embedded chart is nice but simple

Cons
- Limited to only RH ecosystem
- No dedicated ticker UI to track your stocks : have to make a watchlist to act as your ticker
- Buy / Sell doesn’t show percentage gain on options
- No spreads indicator on options
- Chart is limited compared to Tradingview

title: Markets will be closed for day of mourning for Jimmy Carter
body:
President Biden will declare a National Day of Mourning - January 9th for funeral precessions.

Sitting presidents will typically make an address when one of their predecessors passes on, generally declaring a National Day of Mourning on the day of the funeral. That means the federal government will shut down for a day and both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq markets will not trade.

Jimmy Carter passed away at the age of 100 today.

Markets will be closed January 9th.

title: Trading tips - Setup your morning trades
body:
Pro tip to trading. In the morning set up your trades that you want to go after. Let the exit liquidity in the morning get washed out until London Power hour then enter there.

You shouldn’t have to be looking at charts all day. Just open and close one or two trades a day in under an hour. That way the rest of your day is open.

For instance I opened a SPY 1DTE 594 call today and exited at 94% TP.

One lesson I’m teaching myself is don’t diamond hand. If you’re in the green at like 94% just take the win. Sure tomorrow SPY could go even higher but I’m ITM and have my win.

Want to learn more checkout the OA trading workshop we’re doing to introduce people to trading tonight 

https://discord.gg/orangutanarmy

title: My trading style + $U making 💰 this week :)
body:
I have an unusual trading style. I usually invest in the products I use. I use Fey and ChatGPT to help me do my DD and plan out DCA and more.

I like to say I’m more of an investor trader and actually exercise contracts if the strike price goes way above ITM. For example I exercised NVDA at $100, HIMS at $20, HOOD at $20 and $80, and more.

I own shares + do directional options as I’m still studying how to get into futures by reading Implied Voalitity and watching lots of YT videos. I also but some flash cards on trading psychology.

Here’s the trick. Sometimes I like the premium if the strike price goes $4 - $5 above what I put my call on but then I won’t usually exercise. And now I’m less diamond handing my calls and puts when it comes to the theta thunderdome and delta decay. 

Any one else trade like me?

I also tend to keep a journal and am heavily tilted in tech so I’m leaning towards more YieldMaxs and other sectors outside of growth and blue chip style stocks.
